Wearable Sweat Patch for Hydration Monitoring
Abstract: We describe a skin patch that reads hydration from sweat. The main problem is that athletes and clinicians cannot measure hydration without a blood draw. Nurses and sports trainers would use the patch at the point of care. Unlike laboratory assays, our patch gives a result in minutes on a phone. We tested the prototype on 24 volunteers and measured agreement with laboratory results.
Keywords: sweat sensing; hydration; wearable
Results were presented as a poster at the spring symposium on April 4, 2026.
References
[1] Jones, A. Sweat electrolyte sensing. Journal of Sensors 4, 2020.
[2] Park, S. Wearable patches for clinical use. Biosensors 9, 2022.

A Faster Method for Route Planning in Rural Delivery
Abstract: We propose a routing method for delivery vans. The main challenge is that rural routes change daily and current planners are slow. Dispatchers at small delivery companies would use it to replan routes each morning. Unlike existing planners, our method recomputes a full plan in seconds.
